column3: NKJV renders מְרִי (“rebellion”) as “bitter,” following a related reading, and “my hand is heavy” as “My hand is listless.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he would put [his mind] on me” is rendered “He would take note of me.”
Close to the Hebrew; “more than my portion” is rendered “More than my necessary food.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he is in one” is rendered “He is unique.”
Close to the Hebrew; חֻקִּי (“my decree”) is rendered “what is appointed for me.”
NKJV carries the negative into the second line, “He did not hide deep darkness from my face”; the Hebrew can be read “and gloom covers my face.”
